corePages.headline: Die Zahlen von1 bis 20
corePages.bodyGerman:
eins · zwei · drei · vier · fünf · sechs · sieben · acht · neun · zehn
elf · zwölf · dreizehn · vierzehn · fünfzehn · sechzehn · siebzehn · achtzehn · neunzehn · zwanzig
corePages.bodyEnglish: The teen numbers (13–19) are just the unit plus '-zehn': drei+zehn, vier+zehn. Watch the two that change spelling: 'sechs' → 'sechzehn' and 'sieben' → 'siebzehn' (the 'en' drops). 'Eins' loses its s before a noun: 'eine Stunde'.
corePages.culturalTip: Count on your fingers the German way: thumb = 1, little finger = 5. Asking for 'drei' of something while holding up three fingers works everywhere.

corePages.headline: Zahlen21–99: die Einers zuerst
corePages.bodyEnglish: German reverses the tens: you say the ONES first, then 'und', then the TENS.21 is literally 'one and twenty'. The '-zig' ending is a z-sound, and 30 is the odd one out: 'dreißig' with an ß.
corePages.culturalTip: Prices in shops are quoted in full: 'das macht sieben Euro fünfzig' = 7.50. Coins stop at 2 Euro; banknotes start at 5.

corePages.headline: Pfand & Trinkgeld
corePages.bodyEnglish: Bottles and cans carry a 'Pfand' deposit (0.08–0.25 €) refunded when you return them — look for 'mit Pfand' on the label. Tipping is low: round up5–10% and say the amount as you hand it over ('Das macht neun, bitte' while giving a note).
corePages.culturalTip: Card payments under5 € are often refused — carry some cash.

grammar.explanationEnglish: For21–99, German puts the unit first, joins with 'und', then the decade — the reverse of English. 'Einundzwanzig' = one-and-twenty. Everything above99 uses normal order again: 'hundertzwanzig' = 120.
grammar.englishBridge: English: 'twenty-one' (tenner first) → German: 'ein-und-zwanzig' (unit first). Flip the order and you've got it.

practice.explanationEnglish: Unit first, then 'und', then the decade: ein + und + zwanzig = einundzwanzig.
Cents are stated as the full number: 'fünfzig' (50), not 'fünf'. So7.50 = 'sieben Euro fünfzig'.
30 is the exception: 'dreißig' takes an ß, not a z. All other decades end in '-zig'.
